question.problem: At a fruit store, every basket with $40$ apples has $2$ rotten apples, on average. If an employee checks only one apple from each basket, what is the probability that they will find the first rotten apple on the $7$th basket they check? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of baskets checked until a rotten apple is found. On average, the chance of finding a rotten apple is 

$$
p=\frac{2}{40}=0.05.
$$

So, the number of baskets that the employee checks before finding a rotten apple can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.05.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.05).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.05)^{x-1}(0.05) \\  & =(0.95)^{x-1}(0.05)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding the first rotten apple on the $7$th basket is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=7) & =f(7) \\  & =(0.95)^{7-1}(0.05) \\  & =(0.95)^{6}(0.05) \\  & ≈0.037\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
